To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate a new approach to achieve optical loss modulation in an AR HCF by embedding VO2 nanocrystallites into its air holes.
we have demonstrated a new type of optical modulator that operates over a broad spectral range and has a high extinction ratio, by embedding VO2 phase change nanocrystal into an antiresonant fiber.
we fabricate an optical modulator based on the insulator to metal transition of vanadium oxide phase change nanocrystal coated antiresonance fiber.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optical modulation of an AR HCV fiber by the effect of the insulator-to-metal phase transition of VO2 nanocrystal.
the study of the effect of VO2 nanocrystal phase transition in an antiresonic hollow core fiber.
the development of a novel optical fiber based device that can be used for optical modulation in a broad spectral range, and can be operated at room temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VO2 nanocrystal infiltrated AR HCF is a promising platform for the realization of an all-optical switch with a large modulation bandwidth and low power consumption.
the optical modulation by VO2 nanocrystal embedded antiresonant fiber can be a promising candidate for optical modulation in future photonic circuits.
this work is the first to demonstrate a phase change material (PCM)-based optical modulator operating in the ultrabroadband regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we demonstrate a new class of optical modulators based on phase change materials (PCMs), which can operate over an ultrawide spectral range, with a large modulation depth, at low power, and with fast response.
we have developed the first optical fiber that is capable of modulating optical signals in the S+C+band over a broad temperature range.
we demonstrate the first optical loss modulation of an antiresonant waveguide with VO2 nanocrystal coating.

the AR HCF is a promising optical platform for the realization of optical modulators that operate in the near infrared and mid-infrared spectral ranges, where the use of conventional waveguides is limited by the high loss of silica.
VO2 nanocrystal coated AR HCFs are a viable platform for optical modulation over a broad spectral range.
